- Model consistently underestimates prices, especially in the early part of the forecast horizon (first 5–10 days), suggesting a persistent downward bias.
- Forecasts tend to overshoot after sharp price spikes (e.g., 70+ → 72+), then correct sharply — model overreacts to recent highs and fails to capture mean reversion.
- Late-period forecasts (last 5–10 days) are often too low, indicating model struggles to anticipate sustained upward momentum or policy-driven price increases.
- Model exhibits lag in recognizing true price trends — true price increases (e.g., 70→72) are often forecasted too late or not at all.
- Forecasts show a tendency to “smooth” volatility — underestimating volatility spikes and overestimating calm periods, leading to underprediction of price surges.
- Model fails to capture the “tail” of price movements — especially when true prices rise sharply in the final 5–10 days of the forecast window.
- Model often underestimates the impact of policy or market events that drive price increases — especially in the last 10 days of the forecast horizon.
- Forecasts are overly conservative in the early days, then become more aggressive later — suggesting a non-linear adjustment to recent price trends.
